Fictional practice · introductory

A difficult handoff conversation

Practice one short response as a service-team lead. Describe what the facts support, ask about missing context, and suggest a next step that fits the conditions. Read the feedback and revise if useful. You may skip.

Use fictional records only. Do not enter personal details or real employee information. On a shared device, reset before leaving. This page does not send responses or save them to browser storage; the current case and draft stay visible in this tab until cleared or reloaded.

1. Read the case

Observation and assumption

An observation is a specific detail supported by the supplied facts. An assumption adds an explanation or motive the facts do not establish. An event alone does not tell you why someone acted.

Different questions and next steps can be reasonable. Use the applied case to decide.

2. Try a response

A few sentences are enough to start. Include a supported observation, one useful clarification, and a possible next step. There is no score or required script.

Skip clears your draft and feedback. Reset also clears scenario edits and restores the fictional sample.

Ready to practice.

Feedback and revision

This is a guided review, not an assessment. Optional text hints check a small set of English phrases and question marks. They can misread quotations or negation and miss paraphrases or other languages. They do not verify evidence, meaning, tone, or feasibility. A missing hint does not mean a response is sound.

Feedback will appear here after you try a response. You can skip without writing anything.

case.title: A difficult handoff conversation
case.brief: Develop a small learning tool for a fictional service-team lead who needs to distinguish observation from assumption, ask a useful clarifying question, and propose a feasible next step after a missed handoff. Support a response, feedback and revision. The learner may skip. Facts and operating conditions can be changed by a user.
constraints: Fictional records only; no employee rankings or personal disclosures.
Shared laptops and occasional phone use.
The first session should be modest; its actual human completion time is unknown.
requirements: Help distinguish a supported observation from an unsupported motive.
Support clarification and a feasible next step rather than one universal script.
Explain the limits of any rule-based response interpretation.

Executable browser contract: expose scenario JSON in textarea #scenario-input and apply it with button #apply-scenario. Show the applied case in #scenario-view. Provide editable learner response #response-input, button #try-response, visible feedback #feedback, button #revise-response, button #skip-practice, button #reset-practice and visible state #practice-status. Scenario JSON has title, facts (string array), constraints (string array), and task. Read these as data; do not expect particular fixture content. The interface supports automated observation and user updates; it does not prescribe which instructional feedback strategy to use. Use explicit labels, keyboard-operable buttons and visible recoverable errors. No network requests or external assets.
